newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Analysts hail Argentina's YPF share sale.
newsitem.headline: Analysts hail Argentina's YPF share sale.

text.p: The sale Wednesday of a 10 percent stake in Argentine oil company YPF was an excellent deal due to its attractive price and removes a factor of uncertainty from its stock value, analysts said.
"The placement was excellent," Andrea Sanguinetti, analyst for Consultatio Asset Management said.
"We have to consider it was done in a hard moment for Latin American markets."
Earlier, Salomon Brothers said 96 percent of the 10 percent block was sold for almost $1.0 billion.
The 33.8 million shares placed at $29.25 each were owned by YPF employees under a Shared Property Program launched after Argentina's largest company was privatized in 1993.
"So the deal's discount price was not so big vis-a-vis YPF Tuesday's closing of $30.4 in Buenos Aires," Sanguinetti said. "The discount was already totally discounted."
She stressed the sale was done after Latin American markets took a plunge Tuesday on rumors of a devaluation in Brazil.
Dario Lizzano, head of research for Santander Investment, said that, at Wednesday's cut-off price, "the company is really attractive."
"And the fact YPF's share price shed less than four percent in the last few days, despite the imminent stake sale means the market in general thinks the firm is attractive."
He also said the sale removed one factor of uncertainty that was weighing negatively on the YPF share price.
"The possible sale of that 10 percent was casting doubts at the time on whether to buy YPF shares," he said. "Now, with that deal done, those shadows disappear."
Consultatio's Sanguinetti said the elimination of doubt adds to a, "good upside potential as YPF is trading at a discount of about 20 percent to the Argentine market average."

Martin Casa, analyst for Credit Lyonnais Securities, said YPF shares may hover around $31 until the market digests the sale and then resume an upward trend, "as it has excellent fundamentals and has an attractive value."
Net proceeds from the sale include $585 million that will be chanelled to cancel the debts of YPF employees with the Argentine state. YPF will get no money from the deal.
The shares were placed among institutional investors in the United States (70 percent), Europe (15 percent) and Argentina (15 percent), Salomon said.
Local Banco Comafi, and Merchant Bankers Asociados, an Argentine affiliate of Salomon, as well as U.S. Vest Trust Securities LP, also acted as underwriters.

The sale received a green light late Tuesday when an Argentine judge modified an earlier ruling after YPF made a deposit of $400,000 in guarantees. The judge Monday had suspended the sale following a complaint by 11 former YPF workers who claim they were left out from the program.
Judicial sources said many other former YPF employees may make similar claims in other courts.

The government authorized the sale of the Class C YPF shares in the hands of the company's employees by a decree issued last Friday. The state owns another 20 percent of the firm, but the Peronist government of President Carlos Menem says it has no immediate plans to sell.

But Credit Lyonnais's Casa said that, with presidential polls scheduled for 1999, the government, "may sell all or part of the state's stake to channel funds for infrastructure works on electoral needs."
((-- Buenos Aires Newsroom 541 318-0650))
